Plot a context tree

Source: R/plot.R
plot.transitiontrees.Rd

plot() draws a fitted context tree. A context tree organizes the histories that precede each state: the root holds the overall distribution of states; each child extends its parent's history by one earlier state; and every node carries the distribution of the next state given that history. A drawing of the tree shows which histories occur often enough to be modeled, how far back the model's memory reaches along each branch, and where branches stop because a longer history was too rare or, after pruning, added nothing to the prediction.

Four drawings are available. "horizontal" (the default) is a left-to-right tree with depth on the x-axis; each node is labeled with its full history and, by default, its most likely next state and that state's probability, and is filled by the most recent state of the history. "dendrogram" is a radial tree with the root at the center, each node filled by the state its depth adds to the history. "icicle" is a sunburst: rings are depths, the angular width of an arc is proportional to the summed count of the deepest histories beneath it, and the fill is the state the ring adds to the history. "interactive" is a visNetwork widget with draggable nodes and a tooltip that gives each node's count and full next-state distribution. In the node-link drawings, node size is the count of the history and edge width the count of the child history. The first three drawings are ggplot objects; the interactive one is an htmlwidget.

The context tree reads backwards in time: every history ends at the moment of prediction. For the forward view, sequences followed from their first state, use plot_trajectories(). The next-state probabilities of many pathways are compared more easily in plot_pathways() or plot_distributions(), and differences between two groups in plot_difference().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'transitiontrees'
plot(
  x,
  style = c("horizontal", "dendrogram", "icicle", "interactive"),
  point_size_range = NULL,
  edge_size_range = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A transitiontrees object.

style

"horizontal" (default), "dendrogram", "icicle" or "interactive".

point_size_range

Smallest and largest node size. Default NULL: c(4, 14) for "horizontal", c(5, 16) for "dendrogram", c(10, 45) pixels for "interactive". Not used by "icicle".

edge_size_range

Thinnest and thickest edge. Default NULL: c(0.3, 2.5) for the static drawings, c(1, 10) pixels for "interactive". Not used by "icicle".

...

Options of the chosen drawing. "horizontal": show_prediction (default TRUE) adds the most likely next state to each label. "icicle": label_min_fraction (default 0.03) and label_abbrev_fraction (default 0.08), the arc shares below which a label is omitted or abbreviated; abbrev_len (default 2) or abbrev_fun (default NULL) for the abbreviation; gap_size (default 5) and gap_size_within (default 0.3), the widths of the white lines between first-level wedges and between arcs; jitter (default 0.04) and jitter_seed (default 1), a small random variation of the outer edge (0 for none). "interactive": width and height of the widget.

Value

A ggplot object for "horizontal", "dendrogram" and "icicle"; a visNetwork htmlwidget for "interactive".

Conditions

transitiontrees_empty_result

(error) the tree has no nodes.

transitiontrees_missing_package

(error) "interactive" without the visNetwork package installed.

See also

plot.transitiontrees_group for one plot per group; plot_trajectories() for the forward tree; plot_pathways(), plot_distributions() and plot_pruning() for next-state distributions.

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 2)
plot(tree)

plot(tree, show_prediction = FALSE)

plot(tree, style = "dendrogram")

plot(tree, style = "icicle")

if (requireNamespace("visNetwork", quietly = TRUE)) {
  widget <- plot(tree, style = "interactive")
}
